newsitem.title: USA: Bond lawyers criticize IRS yield burning strategy.
newsitem.headline: Bond lawyers criticize IRS yield burning strategy.

text.p: Bond lawyers said the IRS should take action against the bond dealers responsible for "yield burning" rather than the municipalities that innocently enter into such "rigged" bond deals.

"(If) Treasury is concerned that a particular bidding procedure may be rigged or tainted, we suggest that Treasury penalize those engaged in the flawed bidding," the National Association of Bond Lawyers said in a 16-page letter to the Internal Revenue Service last week.
Lawyers urged IRS to provide innocent bond issuers a "safe harbor" from federal action if they relied on qualified experts to advise them on proper yield levels for refundings.
NABL said Congress armed IRS in 1989 with an effective penalty against bond firms that contribute to tax code violations when they do tax-exempt bond deals.

"By ignoring the availability of the penalty, IRS is adding complex new rules rather than attempting to enforce existing rules," David Walton, chairman of NABL's arbitrage and rebate committee, said in the letter.
If the 1989 penalty does not get the job done, then Treasury should ask IRS to strengthen it, said Walton, a former attorney advisor in Treasury's tax legislative counsel's office.

Walton was responding to a rule proposed by IRS June 26 that tells state and local governments how to invest bond proceeds so the reinvestment does not violate federal restrictions on arbitrage profits.
